probe: G0-v2 all-tag-reward ablation (closes the tag-reward family)
status: FROZEN — thresholds declared before the first probe run; do not edit after results exist
question: If tags provide zero direct reward of any kind, does PPO stop discovering tag-farming attractors?

competence_definition.measured_on: held-out TASK_HEALTH panel, seeds 9300000-9300002, opponents OP6/OP9/OP12

alignment_gate.requirement: no reward channel may rise in magnitude while task performance falls

prior_structural_finding_to_re_test.observation: across EVERY run so far -- collapsed and competent alike -- the terminal outcome is 1.4%-1.9% of total absolute reward mass, and reward_failure dominates at 47%-87%
prior_structural_finding_to_re_test.implication: the objective may be a rounding error in the reward signal regardless of which shaping term is being ablated
prior_structural_finding_to_re_test.note: this was measured retrospectively before this probe launched and is recorded here so it cannot be presented afterwards as a post-hoc discovery

outcome_interpretation.best_case: 3/3 alive, >=2/3 competent, no channel rises while task falls -> zero tag reward removes the attractor; tag shaping may be unnecessary because the CONSEQUENCES of a tag already serve the objective
outcome_interpretation.one_seed_farms_another_term: STOP ablations. Evidence is sufficient for a structural reward-budget redesign around objective scale.
outcome_interpretation.all_collapse: STOP ablations. Tag farming was one expression of a deeper shaping problem.
outcome_interpretation.forbidden: reading a partial result and then editing these thresholds; continuing single-constant probes after an outcome that says stop

budget_principle_for_redesign: Across a normal episode the expected CUMULATIVE reward from any farmable shaping behaviour must remain well below the value of accomplishing the objective. Per-event values are not the constraint; cumulative expected value is what PPO optimises.
